blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, the LORD heard it. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "The LORD heard it"] The LORD heard it. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "The LORD heard it"] What they said about Moses and his wife did not stay between them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, Moses had married an Ethiopian woman, a Cushite, from the land south of Egypt. And his own sister and brother started talking.

verses.text: And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

segments.text: Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at that. They started with his wife, and then it turned into, who does he think he is? That is how it goes sometimes. Folks pick at the one he loves when what they really want is his place.

blocks.text: God came down himself and stood up for Moses. Mouth to mouth, God said, I speak with him. Why were you not afraid to speak against my servant? And God never said one word against that Ethiopian woman. Not one.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: And here is the meekness of Moses. His sister spoke against him and against his wife. And the first thing Moses did was pray for her.

verses.text: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.

verses.text: And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The whole camp waited for her. Nobody moved on without Miriam. She was shut out seven days, and then she was brought back in.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, this story says two things plain. God does not take it lightly when folks speak against the ones he has chosen. And God did not see anything wrong with a man of God marrying a woman from Africa. The ones who had a problem with it were the ones who got corrected. And even then, the man they wronged prayed for their healing, and the camp waited until they could come home.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Num 12:1-15; God's words read by the narrator; says only what the text says (God rebukes the speakers and says nothing against the wife); no reading of the leprosy as a racial sign.

cultural.note: The Cushite wife defended with dignity; Miriam not demonised, the camp waits for her; 'the LORD heard it' at the turn.
